extracted.intended_audience: users of PARI/GP library: computational number theorists, mathematicians, and developers working with class field and ideal routines
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP functions related to ray class groups, Galois computations, and ideal arithmetic (bnr*, galois*, ideal* and related routines). Describes purpose, arguments, return values, flags, examples, and caveats for each routine.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrchar
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute characters of a ray class group: returns all characters trivial on a subgroup if v omitted; otherwise g and v must match in length, gi must be ideals (in any form), vi rational with denominator dividing the order of gi in the ray class group; g may be given as a matrix of discrete logarithms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN bnrchar(GEN bnr, GEN g, GEN v = NULL). Examples show use with bnr.gen and using matrix form to specify subgroup generators; e(x)=exp(2iπx) used to interpret character values.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrclassno
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the relative degree [L:K] for a class field L defined by A, B, C (types: [bnr], [bnr, subgroup], [bnf, modulus], or [bnf, modulus, subgroup]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If A is a bnf and B a modulus, returns the ray class number modulo B. Can accept an attached bid (with generators) for B to save time. Faster than bnrinit if only the ray class number is needed. Library syntax: GEN bnrclassno0(GEN A, GEN B = NULL, GEN C = NULL) and GEN bnrclassno(GEN bnf, GEN f). See bnrclassnolist for multiple moduli.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrclassnolist
rubrics_metrics.description: Given bnf and a list of moduli (as from ideallist/ideallistarch), output the list of class numbers of the corresponding ray class groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output is a vector aligned with the list; use bnrclassno for single class number (more efficient). Examples show extracting finite parts of conductors and checking individual class numbers with bnrclassno. Library syntax: GEN bnrclassnolist(GEN bnf, GEN list).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrconductor
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the conductor f of the subfield of a ray class field defined by [A,B,C] (types as in bnrclassno).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag determines output: 0 -> f; 1 -> [f, Clf, H] with ray class group Clf and subgroup H; 2 -> [f, bnr(f), H] with bnr structure. Instead of subgroup H, accept a character χ given as components relative to bnr.gen; returns conductor of Ker χ (flag 0), or [f, Clf, χf] (flag 1), or [f, bnr(f), χf] (flag 2). Library syntax: GEN bnrconductor0(GEN A, GEN B = NULL, GEN C = NULL, long flag) and GEN bnrconductor(GEN bnr, GEN H, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrconductorofchar
rubrics_metrics.description: Obsolete wrapper to compute conductor of a character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bnrconductor instead. Library syntax: GEN bnrconductorofchar(GEN bnr, GEN chi).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrdisc
rubrics_metrics.description: Output discriminant and signature data [N, r1, D] for a class field L over K specified by A,B,C, with bitwise-flag controlling absolute vs relative data and modulus-check behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bit 1 unset -> absolute data related to L/Q: N=[L:Q], r1=#real places of L, D=disc(L/Q); bit 1 set -> relative data: N=[L:K], r1=#real places of K unramified in L, D=relative discriminant ideal. Bit 2 set -> if modulus is not conductor of L, return 0. Library syntax: GEN bnrdisc0(GEN A, GEN B = NULL, GEN C = NULL, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrdisclist
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute list of discriminants and related invariants of Abelian extensions of a number field bnf by increasing modulus norm up to bound, optionally restricting Archimedean ramification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two syntaxes: (bnf, bound, {arch}) or (bnf, list) where list from ideallist/ideallistarch. Output v where v[k] is vector of invariants for ideals of norm k. If arch specified: w entries are [m, d, r, D] (m = prime factorization of modulus, d = absolute degree, r = #real places of L, D = factorization of absolute discriminant), set d=r=D=0 if m not finite part of a conductor. If arch omitted, all t=2^r1 possible Archimedean values are taken and components list [m, [[d1,r1,D1],...]]. Prime ideals encoding and bnfdecodemodule for decoding explained. Use bnrclassno or bnrdisc for single fields (more efficient). Library syntax: GEN bnrdisclist0(GEN bnf, GEN bound, GEN arch = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrgaloisapply
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply an automorphism (given by matrix mat) to a congruence subgroup H (given as HNF matrix) of a bnr structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute matrix with bnrgaloismatrix. Library syntax: GEN bnrgaloisapply(GEN bnr, GEN mat, GEN H).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrgaloismatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the matrix of action of an automorphism aut of the base field on the generators of the ray class field bnr.gen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: aut may be polynomial, algebraic number, vector of automorphisms, or a Galois group (in latter case returns vector of matrices for aut.gen). See bnrisgalois for example. Library syntax: GEN bnrgaloismatrix(GEN bnr, GEN aut). For polynomial/algebraic number use GEN bnrautmatrix(GEN bnr, GEN aut).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrinit
rubrics_metrics.description: Initialize data linked to the ray class group structure for a modulus f over bnf (including computations of class group structure and optional generators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input bnf and modulus f (or attached bid with generators). Result has members: .bnf, .mod, .bid, .clgp, .no, .cyc, .gen (generators only if flag=1). bnr.bnf.* accesses underlying class group members; bnr.bid.* accesses (ZK/f)^*. If flag=0 (default), generators not computed (saves time) and bnr.gen will error. If flag=1, generators are computed. Library syntax: GEN bnrinit0(GEN bnf, GEN f, {flag = 0}). Recommend using GEN Buchray(GEN bnf, GEN module, long flag) with named or-ed flags nf_GEN and nf_INIT instead of numeric flags.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrisconductor
rubrics_metrics.description: Faster test whether a given modulus is the conductor of the class field (returns 1 if conductor, 0 otherwise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slightly faster than bnrconductor when character/subgroup is not primitive. Library syntax: long bnrisconductor0(GEN A, GEN B = NULL, GEN C = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrisgalois
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether the class field attached to subgroup H is Galois over the subfield fixed by gal (given by galoisinit output or matrices from bnrgaloismatrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes the ray class field attached to bnr is Galois (not checked). Using precomputed matrices (bnrgaloismatrix) is faster than passing gal directly. Library syntax: long bnrisgalois(GEN bnr, GEN gal, GEN H). Examples show computing congruence subgroups of small degree that are Galois over Q and recommend precomputing matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrisprincipal
rubrics_metrics.description: Solve the discrete logarithm problem in the ray class group with respect to bnr.gen for an ideal x coprime to modulus f; returns components of x on generators and (optionally) a principal element congruent to 1 mod^* f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag=1, return 2-component vector [v1, α] where v1 are discrete log components and α such that x = α * product(gj^vj). If flag=0, returns only v1; in that case bnr need not contain generators (can be created with bnrinit(...,0)). Library syntax: GEN bnrisprincipal(GEN bnr, GEN x, long flag). Alternative wrappers: isprincipalray(GEN bnr, GEN x) for flag=0; use nf_GEN to get generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrrootnumber
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the Artin root number W(χ) (complex number of modulus 1) attached to an Artin L-function L(s,χ) for a character χ over bnr; flag=1 can be used when character is primitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition: Λ(1−s,χ)=W(χ)Λ(s,χ) where Λ is the completed L-function. Example usage demonstrates constructing χ by components relative to bnr.gen and interpreting roots of unity ζj = e^{2iπ/Nj} using bnr.cyc. Library syntax: GEN bnrrootnumber(GEN bnr, GEN chi, long flag, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrstark
rubrics_metrics.description: Find a relative equation for the class field corresponding to a bnr modulus and optional congruence subgroup using Stark units (requires totally real base and class field; main variable of bnr must not be x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When base field is Q, simpler galoissubcyclo is used. Routine needs to find auxiliary conductor which may not exist (or may be too large) and may return vector of polynomials whose compositum is needed by user. If computation too large, errors (example shows need for huge coefficients). Suggest trying rnfkummer as fallback. Library syntax: GEN bnrstark(GEN bnr, GEN subgroup = NULL, long prec). Post-processing often done with rnfpolredabs for reduced polynomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: dirzetak
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the first b coefficients of the Dedekind zeta function of a number field nf as a Dirichlet series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN dirzetak(GEN nf, GEN b).

rubrics_metrics.name: factornf (obsolete)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obsolete wrapper to factor a univariate polynomial x over a number field defined by polynomial t; use nffactor instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: factornf reduces to factorization over Q (Trager’s trick); nffactor uses van Hoeij’s method and is generally faster. Main variable of t must be lower priority than that of x; if non-rational number field elements occur as coefficients of x, variable of these polmods must match main variable of t. Examples show correct and incorrect usages and error messages. Library syntax: GEN polfnf(GEN x, GEN t).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoischardet
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a galoisinit structure gal and a character χ (as in galoischartable output), return the degree-1 character det ρ as the list det ρ(g) for representatives of conjugacy classes (same ordering as galoisconjclasses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polynomial variable interpreted as o-th root of 1 (o given). Example shows trivial character and listing for all characters. Library syntax: GEN galoischardet(GEN gal, GEN chi, long o).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoischarpoly
rubrics_metrics.description: Return list of characteristic polynomials det(1 − ρ(g)T) for a representation ρ with character χ, evaluated on conjugacy class representatives (same ordering as galoisconjclasses); polynomial variable interpreted as o-th root of 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show use with galoischartable outputs. Library syntax: GEN galoischarpoly(GEN gal, GEN chi, long o).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoischartable
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the character table of group G from a galoisinit structure gal (or a t_VEC of permutations closed under products), returning [M,e] where M is square matrix size N (#conjugacy classes) giving character values as polynomials in y, and e≥1 is integer specifying root-of-unity order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each column corresponds to an irreducible character, ordered by increasing dimension with first column trivial character. Each row corresponds to conjugacy class ordered by galoisconjclasses; first row is identity and entries give χ(1). Values M[i,j] are polynomials in y interpreted as lift of Mod(y, polcyclo(e,'y')). e divides exponent of group and chosen minimally (e=1 for characters over Q). Note M is transpose of usual orientation; examples provided. Library syntax: GEN galoischartable(GEN gal).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisconjclasses
rubrics_metrics.description: Return list of conjugacy classes of the underlying group from galoisinit output, ordered consistently with galoischartable (trivial class first).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts subgroups from galoissubgroups. Examples illustrate permutation orders and counts. Library syntax: GEN galoisconjclasses(GEN gal).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisexport
rubrics_metrics.description: Export underlying permutation group of a galoisinit structure as a string suitable for GAP (flag omitted or 0) or Magma (flag=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to compute IdGroup in GAP to identify abstract group. Accepts subgroups from galoissubgroups. Example shows piping to GAP to get group index. Library syntax: GEN galoisexport(GEN gal, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisfixedfield
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute fixed field of gal by automorphisms perm (element, vector of elements, or subgroup), returning polynomial P and root x (and optionally factorization F) describing fixed field; guarantees P squarefree modulo gal.p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flags: 0 or omitted -> [P,x]; flag=1 -> P only; flag=2 -> [P,x,F] where F is factorization of gal.pol over field defined by P with variable v representing root (priority constraints). Example demonstrates computing fixed field and factorization; library syntax: GEN galoisfixedfield(GEN gal, GEN perm, long flag, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisgetgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Query galpol package for number of isomorphism classes of groups of order a (if b omitted) or return group of order a with index b in GAP4 Small Group library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN galoisgetgroup(long a, long b). Also available: GEN galoisnbpol(long a) when b omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisgetname
rubrics_metrics.description: Query galpol for descriptive string of group of order a and index b in GAP4 Small Group library (strings via GAP StructureDescription).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple groups may share same name. Example lists names of groups of order 12. Library syntax: GEN galoisgetname(long a, long b).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisgetpol
rubrics_metrics.description: Query galpol for a polynomial with Galois group isomorphic to GAP4(a,b), optionally totally real (s=1) or totally complex (s=2); returns [pol, den] where den is denominator of nfgaloisconj(pol).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If b and s omitted, return number of isomorphism classes of groups of order a. Passing den to galoisinit or nfgaloisconj speeds computation. Library syntax: GEN galoisgetpol(long a, long b, long s). Also GEN galoisnbpol(long a) when b,s omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisidentify
rubrics_metrics.description: Return isomorphism class [o,i] (order and index in GAP4 Small Group library) of abstract group underlying a galoisinit structure (or subgroup from galoissubgroups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited to degree ≤127 (some larger 'easy' orders supported). Output mirrors GAP's IdGroup; for larger groups, use galoisexport and GAP4. Library syntax: GEN galoisidentify(GEN gal).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisinit
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute Galois group and auxiliary data for fixed field K/Q defined by polynomial pol (monic irreducible in Z[X] or nfinit output). Requires extension to be Galois with 'weakly' super-solvable (WKSS) Galois group; returns 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm based on Allombert (2001). Returns 8-component vector gal with fields: pol, [p,e,q], p-adic roots, inverse Vandermonde, denominator multiple, group (permutations), generating subset, relative orders. Properties characterize WKSS structure and generator orders; unique expression of any x in G by relative exponents given. den (if present) must be suitable for gal[5]. Library syntax: GEN galoisinit(GEN pol, GEN den = NULL). galoisinit is prerequisite for many galois* routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisisabelian
rubrics_metrics.description: Test if galoisinit output gal is abelian: return 0 if not abelian; if flag=0 return HNF matrix over gal.gen when abelian, if flag=1 return 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also accepts subgroups from galoissubgroups. Library syntax: GEN galoisisabelian(GEN gal, long flag = 0).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisisnormal
rubrics_metrics.description: Return 1 if a subgroup subgrp (from galoissubgroups) is normal in gal, else 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also accepts subgroups from galoissubgroups. Library syntax: long galoisisnormal(GEN gal, GEN subgrp).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoispermtopol
rubrics_metrics.description: Given gal (galoisinit) and permutation perm (or vector/matrix recursively), return the polynomial defining the Galois automorphism attached to perm as output by nfgaloisconj.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: galoispermtopol(G, G[6])~ is equivalent to nfgaloisconj(pol) when degree >= 2. Library syntax: GEN galoispermtopol(GEN gal, GEN perm).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoissubcyclo
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute subextension of Q(ζ_n) fixed by subgroup H ⊂ (Z/nZ)^*, using Kronecker–Weber: supports N as integer, znstar output, or bnrinit output representing ray class group; various H encodings supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation of (N,H) depends on type of N: integer -> n=N and H generator(s); znstar output or bnrinit output -> H can be matrix (HNF left divisor of SNF) giving generators in terms of N.gen. Beware: when infinite place does not divide module, H is understood relative to N and may be subgroup of quotient by {±1}. fl flag: 0 -> compute polynomial in variable v defining subfield; 1 -> compute only conductor (module); 2 -> return [pol, N] with both polynomial and conductor. Helper subcyclo function provided to compute all subfields (optionally exact degree). Library syntax: GEN galoissubcyclo(GEN N, GEN H = NULL, long fl, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoissubfields
rubrics_metrics.description: Output all subfields of a Galois group G by applying galoisfixedfield to all subgroups; flag semantics same as galoisfixedfield.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN galoissubfields(GEN G, long flag = 0, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoissubgroups
rubrics_metrics.description: Output all subgroups of a Galois group gal as vectors [gen, orders] where gen generates subgroup and orders are relative orders; cardinality is product of relative orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such subgroup vectors can be used in many galois* commands (galoisisabelian, galoissubgroups, galoisexport, galoisidentify). To get fixed field of subgroup sub use galoisfixedfield(gal, sub[1]). Library syntax: GEN galoissubgroups(GEN G).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealadd
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute sum of two ideals x and y in number field nf, returning result in HNF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments must be ideals (square t_MAT). Examples show constructing ideal generated by 2 and 1+i. This function cannot add arbitrary Z-modules; to add arbitrary Z-modules use mathnf(concat(A,B)). Errors occur if inputs are non-square matrices or matrices not representing OK-modules; examples show non-sense results in such cases. Library syntax: GEN idealadd(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealaddtoone
rubrics_metrics.description: Given coprime integral ideals x and y (any form), return [a,b] with a∈x, b∈y and a+b=1; alternative syntax accepts vector of ideals summing to ZK and returns vector e with e[i]∈x[i] and sum e[i]=1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealaddtoone0(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealappr
rubrics_metrics.description: Given fractional ideal x, produce element α in nf such that for primes p where vp(x)≠0, vp(α)=vp(x), and vp(α)≥0 for other p; x may be given as prime ideal factorization (allowing zero exponents) producing α matching valuations on occurring primes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag argument deprecated/ignored. Library syntax: GEN idealappr0(GEN nf, GEN x, long flag). Use GEN idealappr(GEN nf, GEN x) (flag ignored).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealachinese
rubrics_metrics.description: Solve Chinese remainder problem for ideals: given prime ideal factorization x and vector y of target residues, compute b with vp(b - y_p) ≥ vp(x) for primes in x and vp(b) ≥ 0 for other p; supports sign conditions for real embeddings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: x may be given as [x, s] where s is vector of signs si∈{−1,0,1} fixing sign of real embeddings; if y omitted return a structure usable for repeated solves more efficiently (idealachineseinit). Examples show performance improvements when reusing init structure. Library syntax: GEN idealchinese(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y = NULL) and GEN idealchineseinit(GEN nf, GEN x) when y=NULL.

rubrics_metrics.name: idealcoprime
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two integral ideals x and y in nf, return β such that β·x is an integral ideal coprime to y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealcoprime(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealdiv
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute quotient x·y^{-1} of two ideals x and y in nf, returning result in HNF; optional flag=non-zero assumes quotient is integral, enabling faster algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag non-zero (flag=1) algorithm cheaply removes maximal ideals above rational primes where vp(N x)=vp(N y), making it faster when quotient norm is small. Syntax variants: GEN idealdiv0(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y, long flag), GEN idealdiv(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y) (flag=0), GEN idealdivexact(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y) (flag=1).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealfactor
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor ideal x into prime ideal powers in nf; output format similar to factor, primes in form of idealprimedec output. Optional lim restricts to primes above rational primes < lim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show factoring ideals given as HNF matrices and factor with limit. Note this gp-specific wrapper naming; recommended direct usage: GEN idealfactor(GEN x) or GEN idealfactor_limit(GEN x, ulong lim). Library syntax: GEN gpidealfactor(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN lim = NULL) (gp interface only).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealfactorback
rubrics_metrics.description: Recover ideal corresponding to a factorization f (integer 1 corresponds to empty factorization); if e present, f and e must be vectors of same length and resulting ideal is product f[i]^{e[i]}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealfactorback(GEN nf, GEN f, GEN e = NULL, long flag = 0).
